title: ack
description: Daemon -> client handshake response. accepted=false carries an error and ends the session. This is the ONLY place a client learns what robot it is talking to: see `descriptor` (what it can move) and `capabilities` (what verbs it honours). Clients MUST derive behaviour from those, never from `model`.

model.description: ADVISORY ONLY. The robot's model/generation label (e.g. "L2", "L3"). Provided so logs, dataset provenance and bug reports can name the hardware. Clients MUST NOT branch behaviour on this value -- branch on `descriptor` and `capabilities` instead, so a new model works against an unmodified client. Deliberately not an enum: enumerating models here would mean a schema edit per model, which is exactly the coupling this field exists to avoid. Absent on robots predating the field.

capabilities.description: Optional verbs this robot honours, beyond the always-present core (control jog, control action, command, telemetry). A client MUST treat an absent capability as unsupported, and MUST ignore an unrecognised entry rather than failing. This exists because capability differences are NOT expressible as DOFs: a descriptor cannot say whether absolute lift targets are accepted or whether two-way audio exists. Known values: "task_jog" (cylindrical/task-space arm jog), "leader_action_deg" (absolute leader-arm degrees), "lift_targets" (absolute <side>_lift.pos height targets in mm), "record" (dataset recording verbs), "policy_stream", "call" (two-way audio), "perception". Absent field means UNKNOWN, not none -- robots predating the field must be probed or assumed legacy. WHO FILLS THIS: it is a UNION built along the path. A daemon lists what it itself honours (task_jog, leader_action_deg, lift_targets); a bridge APPENDS what it adds on top (record, policy_stream, call) before forwarding, because the daemon cannot know whether a bridge in front of it does two-way audio. On a merged stack like the L3 gateway one process fills the whole list. A client therefore sees one flat list and must not infer which component provides a given capability.

norm_mode.description: Normalization mode of all .pos values in state/action.

descriptor.description: What this robot physically is. OPTIONAL, and its ABSENCE is meaningful: a robot that sends no descriptor is a legacy unit whose DOF vocabulary the client must already know (the L2 daemon is one -- see MODELS.md). Present-and-populated is the only case in which a client may drive DOFs it did not know about in advance.

joints.description: Every drivable "<motor>.pos" key. This is the authoritative joint vocabulary; a client must build its keymap from this rather than from a compiled-in list.

base.description: Base DOFs in the TELEMETRY namespace ("x.vel", "theta.vel"). WARNING: this is NOT the jog namespace. A control jog addresses the base as {"base":{"linear":r,"angular":r}} -- see control.json. The two vocabularies are different on purpose (telemetry reports measured axis velocities; jog expresses normalized drive intent) and confusing them yields a frame the robot parses as a full stop.

aux.description: Non-arm actuators addressable by jog, e.g. "left_lift"/"right_lift". A robot with lifts MUST list them here; leaving this empty while accepting lift jog makes the lifts undiscoverable and is a defect.

cameras.description: Camera roles, for logging and diagnostics ONLY. This does NOT drive video: the robot sends one composited H.264 track and describes its tiling in camera_layout.json, which is authoritative and independent of this field. Do not derive a layout from this list.

ranges.description: Authoritative [min, max] per "<name>.pos". Values outside are CLAMPED robot-side, never rejected, so use these to scale input rather than to pre-validate. A joint absent from this map has no advertised range and a client must not invent one.
